items.stem: A 1.5 kg mass on a horizontal spring oscillates in SHM with amplitude 0.025 m. Its period is T = 1.03 s. Calculate the spring stiffness k.
items.workedSolution: Rearranging T = 2π√(m / k) gives k = 4π²m / T² = 4π²(1.5) / (1.03)² = 56.0 N m⁻¹.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Inverts m / T² when rearranging the period equation.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Fails to square 2π / T when rearranging T = 2π√(m / k), computing 2πm / T instead of 4π²m / T².

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 4π² and computes m / T².

items.stem: A light ray in air (n₀ = 1) hits a parallel-sided flint glass plate (n₁ = 1.65, thickness 0.03 m) in air. It enters at 26° to the normal. How far along the exit face is the exit point shifted from the entry normal?
items.workedSolution: Inside the flint glass slab, sin θ₁ = (1 sin 26°) / 1.65, giving θ₁ = 15.4°. The transverse shift along the exit face is Δy = t₁ tan θ₁ = 0.03 × tan 15.41° = 0.00827 m.

items.stem: A light beam in diamond (n₁ = 2.42) meets a flat boundary with air (n₂ = 1). The angle of incidence is 33° to the normal, and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Calculate the angle through which the beam is turned at the boundary.
items.workedSolution: Since sin θ_c = 1 / 2.42 gives θ_c = 24.4° and θ₁ = 33° > θ_c, total internal reflection occurs with θ_r = 33°. The angular deviation from the original forward direction is δ = 180° − 2(33°) = 114°.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies TIR (θ₁ > θ_c = 24.4°) and computes δ = 180° − 2θ₁ = 114° (A).

items.stem: A 0.15 kg brass bob hangs on a 0.85 m light wire and swings with arc amplitude 0.238 m. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the maximum tension in the wire at the lowest point.
items.workedSolution: With ω = √(g / L) = √(9.81 / 0.85), peak speed v_max = ω x₀ = 0.809 m s⁻¹. At the lowest point, T_cord = m(g + v_max² / L) = 1.59 N.

markScheme.criterion: Uses v_max = ω x₀ and T_cord = mg + mv_max² / L = 1.59 N (A).

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Equates cord tension at the lowest point to static weight mg, ignoring the upward centripetal force mv_max² / L.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Subtracts the centripetal force mv_max² / L from mg instead of adding it at the bottom of the arc.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates only the net radial centripetal force mv_max² / L rather than the total cord tension.

markScheme.criterion: Finds total SHM energy E_tot = 17.8 mJ.

options.distractorRationale: Dispersion spreads arrival times of guided rays; it is distinct from bend-loss refraction.

options.text: When pulses spread in time, the frequency of the laser doubles inside the core
options.distractorRationale: Wave frequency remains constant across optical media.

options.label: D
options.text: When pulses spread in time, data rate increases because longer pulses carry more energy
options.distractorRationale: Overlapping pulses merge 1s and 0s, forcing lower bit rates or shorter fibre sections.

items.stem: A 0.6 kg mass hangs from a vertical spring of stiffness 100 N m⁻¹. It then oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.024 m, where g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the static equilibrium extension Δx_eq of the spring?
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.6 × 9.8) / 100 = 0.0588 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

items.stem: An object of mass 0.6 kg moves in SHM with amplitude 0.14 m and ω = 30 rad s⁻¹, with a marker at x = 0.035 m. Find the frequency f_E of its kinetic energy oscillations.
items.workedSolution: Mechanical frequency f = ω / (2π) = 30 / (2π) = 4.775 Hz. Because kinetic energy reaches a maximum twice per mechanical period, f_E = 2f = ω / π = 9.55 Hz.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Gives the mechanical displacement frequency f = ω / (2π) instead of recognizing that E_k ∝ cos²(ωt) oscillates at 2f.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Halves the mechanical frequency instead of doubling it.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Calculates 2ω in rad s⁻¹ without dividing by 2π to convert to hertz.

items.stem: An astronomer sets a refracting telescope to normal adjustment to view a distant nebula with a relaxed eye. Which statement best describes the final image seen?
items.workedSolution: With $F_o$ and $F_e$ coincident, rays leave the eyepiece parallel so the observer sees a virtual inverted image formed at infinity.

items.stem: The graph shows acceleration against displacement for an object in SHM. It oscillates at 6 Hz with amplitude 0.05 m. Using a = −ω²x, calculate the signed acceleration at x = 0.0225 m.
items.workedSolution: Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 2π(6) = 37.70 rad s⁻¹. By the defining SHM equation, a = −ω²x = −(37.70)²(0.0225) = -32.0 m s⁻².

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates ω = 2πf and obtains -32.0 m s⁻² (D).

items.stem: A 2400 m step-index optical fibre has core index 1.62 and cladding index 1.51. Its end sits in air (n_ext = 1.00), with a 14.4° ray shown, and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Calculate the longest travel time for a guided ray along the fibre.
items.workedSolution: Wave speed in the core is v = c / n_core, and the critical-angle ray travels path length L / sin θ_c = L (n_core / n_clad). Therefore t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.39 × 10⁻⁵ s.

markScheme.criterion: Evaluates t_max = n_core² L / (c n_clad) = 1.39 × 10⁻⁵ s (D).

items.stem: A straight 350 m step-index optical fibre has n_core = 1.48 and n_clad = 1.41. A ray from air (n_ext = 1.00) enters the flat end at θ_in = 42.7° to the axis, so light leaks into the cladding. What is the angle of refraction in the cladding, measured from the wall normal?
items.workedSolution: At entry, sin θ_axis = (1 sin 42.7°) / 1.48 ⇒ θ_axis = 27.3°. The angle to the wall normal is θ_w = 90° − θ_axis = 62.7° (< θ_c = 72.3°). Refracting into the cladding: sin θ_clad = (1.48 sin θ_w) / 1.41, giving θ_clad = 68.9°.

markScheme.criterion: Finds θ_w = 62.7° and refracts into cladding to obtain 68.9° (C).

items.stem: Light of vacuum wavelength 650 nm passes from water (n₁ = 1.33) into diamond (n₂ = 2.42). It hits the flat boundary at 52° to the normal, with vacuum speed 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Calculate its wavelength in diamond.
items.workedSolution: Wave frequency remains unchanged across the boundary, while phase speed decreases to v₂ = c / n₂. Hence λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 650 / 2.42 = 269 nm.

markScheme.criterion: Uses λ₂ = λ₀ / n₂ = 650 / 2.42 to obtain 269 nm (D).

items.stem: A simple pendulum of length 1.15 m has a 0.25 kg bob. It swings with a small arc amplitude of 0.115 m, where g = 9.8 m s⁻². Find its period T.
items.workedSolution: For small angles, T = 2π√(L / g) = 2π√(1.15 / 9.8) = 2.15 s (independent of bob mass).

markScheme.criterion: Obtains 2.15 s using g = 9.8 m s⁻² (B).

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps L / g and g / L inside the square root, computing 2π√(g / L).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Computes the half-period π√(L / g) for a single swing from one extreme to the other rather than a complete cycle.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2πL / g.

items.stem: Which statement identifies a major clinical advantage of flexible fibre-optic endoscopy over exploratory open surgery or X-ray imaging?
items.workedSolution: Flexible endoscopy provides real-time colour optical inspection and keyhole biopsy channels: keyhole internal imaging avoids ionising radiation and reduces surgical trauma.

markScheme.criterion: Identifies that keyhole internal imaging avoids ionising radiation and reduces surgical trauma.

options.text: Direct keyhole internal imaging avoids ionising radiation and reduces surgical trauma, lowering infection risk and shortening hospital recovery.

options.text: Endoscopy penetrates solid bone with high-energy gamma photons to reconstruct three-dimensional CT volumes.

options.text: Endoscopy produces higher magnetic field contrast of deep brain tissue than an MRI scanner.
options.distractorRationale: Endoscopy inspects internal cavity surfaces optically rather than deep closed tissues like the brain.

options.text: Endoscopy requires no illumination because internal organs emit intense visible black-body radiation.
options.distractorRationale: Body tissues at 310 K emit infrared, not visible light, so an illumination bundle is required.

items.stem: A 0.036 m lit object stands 0.75 m in front of a thin diverging lens of focal length −0.3 m. Using the real-is-positive sign convention, find the signed image distance v.
items.workedSolution: For a diverging lens, f = −0.3 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v gives 1/v = −1/0.3 − 1/0.75 = -4.667 m⁻¹, so v = -0.214 m.

markScheme.criterion: Uses negative f = −0.3 m in 1/v = 1/f − 1/u to obtain v = -0.214 m (C).

items.stem: A vertical spring of stiffness 25 N m⁻¹ supports a 0.6 kg mass. The mass oscillates vertically with amplitude 0.032 m, where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the equilibrium extension Δx_eq before oscillation starts.
items.workedSolution: At static equilibrium, upward spring tension balances weight: k Δx_eq = mg ⇒ Δx_eq = (0.6 × 9.81) / 25 = 0.235 m.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Divides mass m directly by spring constant k without multiplying by gravitational field strength g.

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Adds the oscillation amplitude x₀ to mg / k, finding maximum total stretch rather than static equilibrium extension.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts Hooke's law as k / (mg) instead of mg / k.

items.stem: A short-sighted (myopic) patient has an unaided far point of 0.625 m in front of the eye. Using the real-is-positive convention $\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{u} + \frac{1}{v}$, what corrective spectacle lens power is needed to focus distant objects clearly?
items.workedSolution: For a distant object ($u = \infty$), the lens must form a virtual image at the unaided far point ($v = -0.625\text{ m}$). Hence $P = \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{\infty} + \frac{1}{-0.625} = -1.60 D$.

items.stem: A small object of height 0.018 m is held 0.08 m in front of a thin converging lens of focal length 0.1 m. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v in the real-is-positive convention, what is the signed image distance v?
items.workedSolution: Because u = 0.08 m < f = 0.1 m, 1/v = 1/0.1 − 1/0.08 = -2.500 m⁻¹, giving a signed virtual image distance v = -0.400 m.

markScheme.criterion: Computes 1/v = 1/0.1 − 1/0.08 to obtain signed v = -0.400 m (D).

items.stem: The velocity–displacement graph shows an object in SHM with ω = 24 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude x₀ = 0.04 m. Find its speed at x = 0.02 m.
items.workedSolution: Using v = ω√(x₀² − x²) gives v = 24 × √(0.04² − 0.02²) = 0.831 m s⁻¹.

markScheme.criterion: Substitutes into v = ω√(x₀² − x²) to obtain 0.831 m s⁻¹ (B).

items.stem: A 0.16 kg mass oscillates horizontally on a spring of stiffness 18 N m⁻¹. The oscillation amplitude is 0.075 m. Calculate the period T.
items.workedSolution: For an ideal mass-spring oscillator, T = 2π√(m / k) = 2π√(0.16 / 18) = 0.592 s.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Swaps m/k and k/m inside the radical, computing 2π√(k / m) instead of 2π√(m / k).

options.label: C
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and calculates √(m / k) = 1 / ω.

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Omits the square root and evaluates 2π(m / k).

items.stem: A uniform flint glass slab has refractive index 1.65 and thickness 0.065 m. It separates air (n₀ = 1) from ethanol (n₂ = 1.36). A narrow ray enters from air at 28° to the normal. Find the exit angle in ethanol.
items.workedSolution: Across parallel flat boundaries, n₀ sin θ₀ = n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂. Thus sin θ₂ = (1 × sin 28°) / 1.36, giving θ₂ = 20.2°.

markScheme.criterion: Applies Snell invariant n₀ sin θ₀ = n₂ sin θ₂ to obtain θ₂ = 20.2° (A).

items.stem: An optical block is placed in ethanol (n₂ = 1.36). The critical angle at its flat surface is 34.2° to the normal. Find the refractive index n₁ of the block.
items.workedSolution: At the critical angle, n₁ sin θ_c = n₂ sin 90° = n₂, so n₁ = 1.36 / sin 34.2° = 2.42.

markScheme.criterion: Computes n₁ = n₂ / sin θ_c = 1.36 / sin 34.2° = 2.42 (B).

items.stem: A simple pendulum has a 0.15 kg bob on a 2.4 m light string. It swings with small arc amplitude 0.6 m, where g = 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the period T.

options.label: A
options.distractorRationale: Omits the factor of 2π and evaluates √(L / g) = 1 / ω.

options.label: B
options.distractorRationale: Calculates the half-period π√(L / g) instead of the full period 2π√(L / g).

options.label: D
options.distractorRationale: Inverts L / g inside the square root.
